The petitioner assails orders dated 09.01.2025 and 17.05.2025 of Magisterial Court, which orders largely deal with Section 173(8)/156(3) CrPC.

Although the orders impugned in the present petition are interlocutory orders, but learned senior counsel for petitioner contends that since those orders cause grave injustice and are abuse of process, it is a fit case to invoke inherent powers.

Learned senior counsel for petitioner contends as follows.

The petitioner and the complainant de facto (yet to be impleaded) were in a relationship for five years but since parental family of the petitioner did not approve of their getting married, the petitioner expressed inability to continue his relations with her.
That led to the registration of FIR No.425/2023 of PS Rajouri Garden for offences under Section 376/506/34 IPC.
The petitioner was granted anticipatory bail on the basis of certain photographs and WhatsApp chats between the parties.

The impugned order dated 09.01.2025 deals with the application of the petitioner, whereby he sought further investigation,
pointing out that vital pieces of evidence were not collected by the IO.

sentences.text: It is explained by learned senior counsel for petitioner that mobile phone of the petitioner was seized by the IO but mobile phone of the complainant de facto was not seized.

In this regard, the reasoning given by the learned Magistrate is that since the content in mobile phone of complainant de facto is also present in the mobile phone of the petitioner, in view of privacy of complainant de facto, her mobile phone cannot be directed to be seized.
As regards privacy, learned senior counsel for petitioner suggests that redaction of the personal details can be carried out.

Further, it appears that the IO submitted before the learned Magistrate that certain additional facts had come up during further investigation and those facts are required to be probed, but by impugned order dated 17.05.2025, the learned Magistrate curtailed that exercise, directing the IO to confine the investigation to the aspects mentioned in the order dated 09.01.2025.

4. Learned APP accepts notice and submits that even State contemplated to challenge order dated 17.05.2025 which interferes in investigation.
Learned APP on instructions of the IO/SI Meenu submits that till next date they shall not file supplementary chargesheet, though they may continue the investigation.
5. Petitioner is directed to implead the complainant de facto by filing amended memo of parties and notice be issued to her through IO, returnable on 25.08.2025.
6. Copy of this order be sent to the learned Magistrate for information.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J MAY 29, 2025/ry
